questions.question_prompt: You must wait before turning left across oncoming traffic. How should you hold your front wheels?
questions.keyed_answer: Keep them straight until you can turn.
questions.teaching_excerpt: keep your front wheels pointing straight ahead. Your indicator communicates the intended turn; your wheels do not need to point along that intended route while you wait. If a vehicle hits you from behind, front wheels already turned left can direct the pushed car into oncoming traffic. Keeping them straight helps reduce that risk, but cannot guarantee protection in a collision. Begin steering into the turn only when there is a safe opportunity to make it. New York DMV: waiting to turn left Waiting is different from turning. Follow the positioning, signalling and observation requirements above. The wheel-position advice does not create permission to enter or block a junction, ignore a signal, or obstruct someone else's path. Continue observing oncoming traffic, the receiving road, crossings and vehicles behind you while waiting. Recheck the full path before moving. Practice example.
